resources.string: No app can open this link
Ctrl+Space opens Quick Launch from anywhere

Lets Quick Launch open when you press Ctrl+Space on a physical keyboard, from any app. Quick Launch only listens for that key combination. It does not read screen content, observe your activity, or receive any other accessibility events.
Find “Quick Launch keyboard shortcut” under Installed apps. If the switch says “Restricted setting”: open Quick Launch’s App info › ⋮ › Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Tap to enable the keyboard shortcut
Open with Ctrl+Space from any app

Quick Launch uses Android’s Accessibility Service API for one purpose: to notice when you press Ctrl+Space on a physical keyboard while you are in another app, so it can open the search card. Android offers no other way for an app to see a keyboard shortcut before the system handles it.

The service receives only that key combination. It does not read screen content, see what you type, observe your activity in other apps, or receive any other accessibility events. No personal or sensitive data is collected, stored, or shared. This feature is optional and can be turned off at any time in Settings › Accessibility.
Continue to enable “Quick Launch keyboard shortcut” under Settings › Accessibility › Installed apps.
